open_questions: No on_target centroid to rule out blend; inconclusive centroid and neighbours data (closest that could sep 31.9 arcsec) remain but odd/even and depth instability already favour eclipsing binary over planet
dossier.public_summary: The three- to four-fold difference between odd and even dips, plus a large change in depth between sectors and between individual transits, strongly favours a binary system seen at twice the reported period, not a planet. The signal is inconsistent from transit to transit and sector to sector.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ strongly and consistently with ratio 2.1 and 4.145 sigma, indicating twice-the-period eclipsing binary rather than a planet. Vetting rule treats >=4 sigma with real difference as strong binary evidence.
reasons.value: diff_sigma 4.145, depth_odd_ppm 8077 vs depth_even_ppm 3839, depth_ratio 2.1, depth_difference_ppm 4237, sector_oe_same_sign_share 1

reasons.why: Individual transits are inconsistent at extremely low p_consistent and carry signal mostly in top 3 events; same pattern seen in sector depths (71% change with p_constant 0.0004789 even within same source TESS-SPOC). Together with odd/even difference this is eccentric/ellipsoidal variation or a few spurious dips, not a stable planet.
reasons.value: p_consistent 3.4845261743398737e-08, chi2 37.570590421097016 dof 3, 4 transits, share_of_top_3 0.99, outlier depth_ppm 1151 sigma -4.8, sector_depths_by_source verdict changes_within_a_source p_constant 0.0004789 depth_change_pct 71.25 (sector 1 depth_ppm 3278 vs sector 68 depth_ppm 6906)

reasons.why: Planet-like size and flat-bottom shape (v_sigma -2.757) alone do not earn gate2 because flat eclipses can still be small-star grazings and blended binaries; here the binary indicators dominate and ML rank 0.06 supports false positive.
reasons.value: rp_rearth 3.525, duration ratio 1.427, phase_curve amplitude_ppm 726.4, xgboost planet_rank 0.06
